egressOwner: legacy variant: per-connection Tokio sender (RESTREAM_EGRESS_FABRIC unset). fabric variant: RtmpFabricEngine/RtmpShardBackend (RESTREAM_EGRESS_FABRIC=rtmp).
comparison: At real scale (N=1000, matching the Phase 5 exit gate's target order of magnitude), the smoke-scale N=10 capture's ~1.4x fabric CPU regression essentially disappears: CPU avg is 85.31% vs legacy's 83.67% (~1.02x, within noise), while RSS avg is actually 11% *lower* for fabric (287,432KB vs 321,129KB). The one open question this run surfaces: fabric's CPU *peak* is 130.78% vs legacy's 94.32% (~1.39x) despite average parity -- a burst somewhere during the run (most likely the ramp-up phase adding outputs one at a time) that the average smooths over. Both variants delivered all 1000 outputs to progress within timeout; zero error/decode lines in either mediamtx log; restream.log had no warnings or errors in either variant (an empty feed at this point in the ramp means no feed-overrun resync events, unlike the SRT captures at this scale).
scope: Real-scale capture at the project's own target order of magnitude (docs/egress-implementation.md Phase 5 exit gate references 1,000+ healthy RTMP outputs) -- not the full mixed RTMP/RTMPS + bad-neighbor isolation matrix that exit gate ultimately requires, but a meaningful step up from the earlier N=10 smoke-scale capture at this same path (see the sibling vps-6cpu-12gb/ directory).
deviations: Isolated lifecycle (one mediamtx+restream stack per variant, not shared); single measurement point per variant rather than a growth curve; single host sample, not a multi-run statistical distribution.
